result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_bipartite()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if graph is bipartite (2-colorable). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L4135-L4188){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_bipartite() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A graph is bipartite if its nodes can be divided into two independent sets such that every edge connects nodes from different sets. Equivalently, the graph can be colored with two colors such that no adjacent nodes share a color. All trees and forests are bipartite. Graphs with odd-length cycles are not. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph is bipartite, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A simple path is bipartite: ::: {#ceaa0f06 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) # Returns True graph.is_bipartite() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Triangles are not bipartite (odd cycle): ::: {#d16d24b4 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} triangle = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") # Creates odd-length cycle ) # Returns False triangle.is_bipartite() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: :::
